Use set ntp ntp-enabled true ntp-auth-enabled true, in Operational Mode or Candidate Configuration Mode. ntp-enabled takes true or false and defaults to true; ntp-auth-enabled takes true or false and defaults to false, so authentication must be turned on explicitly. The third settable attribute is assignment-method, with values manual, dhcp or both, default both, which selects whether the system uses manually configured or DHCP-supplied NTP values. Verify with show ntp [ntp-enabled] [ntp-auth-enabled] [ntp-active-server] [assignment-method]. For authentication to work you also need keys created with add ntp-key-<key-id> and bound to a server through the ntp-server auth-key-id attribute. The ntp object is system managed and cannot be manually added or deleted.

NTP keys are managed with add / set / show / delete ntp-key-<key-id>, in Operational Mode or Candidate Configuration Mode. The key-type attribute is the hash algorithm used for NTP message digest computation, and the permitted values are sha-1, aes-cmac, sha-256 and md5; there is no default, and key-type is mandatory on add. key-id is a number in the range 1..65534. key-value is a string of length 8..40. is-trusted marks the key as a trusted NTP key, takes true or false, and defaults to false. Example: add ntp-key-2 is-trusted true key-type sha-1 key-value Infinera.

Yes. The ntp-server origin attribute records the NTP address assignment method, with values dhcp (the address was assigned by a DHCP server) and manual (manually configured), default manual. A user can convert a DHCP-configured NTP entry into a manually configured one by changing this attribute: set ntp-server-<ip-address> origin manual. The AID accepts an IPv4 address, an IPv6 address or a DNS domain name. Other settable attributes on the entry are auth-key-id (uint32 or not-applicable, default not-applicable), label (string 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock) and alarm-report-control (allowed, inhibited; default allowed). Note that the ntp assignment-method attribute (manual, dhcp, both; default both) governs which set of configured values the system uses.

Run show ntp-server-status-<ip-address>, for example show ntp-server-status-172.19.13.218. The reach attribute is the reachability indicator: an 8-bit shift register with the most recent probe in the 2^0 position, where the value 377 means all recent probes have been answered. Supporting attributes are when (seconds elapsed since the last packet was received), poll (polling interval in seconds), delay, offset and jitter (all in milliseconds), stratum of the remote peer, refid (reference clock type or address, string 1..32), type (local, unicast, multicast or broadcast), auth-status (ok, yes, bad, none; default none) and condition (values such as sys.peer, reject, candidate). show ntp ntp-active-server tells you which server is currently active.

Syntax is restart [-h] [-f] [<resource-id>] [<type>] [<sub-component>], Operational Mode. If <type> is not given, a warm start is done by default; if <resource-id> is not given, the active controller card is restarted. cold reboots all components and sub-components and is service affecting, with connectivity regained within five minutes; a cold reboot of XMM4 is not service affecting but visibility is lost, while a cold reboot of CHM6, UCM4 and similar is service affecting. warm reboots only the processor of the CHM6, UCM4 and similar and is non service affecting, with connectivity regained within five minutes; on XMM4 it is non-service affecting but visibility is lost for 3 minutes. A third type, shutdown, gracefully shuts the card down. The command prompts for confirmation unless -f is given, and not all cards support all restart types.

set-time is only applicable when time-source is manual, that is, when NTP is not enabled. Since ntp-enabled defaults to true, you must first run set ntp ntp-enabled false, then confirm with show clock time-source that it reads manual rather than ntp. The syntax is set-time [new-time=]<value> in Operational Mode, with -h for help. The value uses a format derived from ISO 8601, combined date and time such as 2017-01-12T10:22:25Z, where Z denotes UTC; a non-UTC timezone is allowed by supplying +/-hh:mm instead of Z, for example set-time 2021-04-01T18:46:44+03:00. Read the current time back with the time command, which reports it using the system configured timezone, not the timezone used in the set-time command.

Yes: status equipment, in Operational Mode. The Equipment dashboard summarises all equipment in the system with relevant details including temperature sensors and power values, plus generic status (presence or absence, oper state, alarms). It lists the chassis, the cards per chassis with their subtype, and the toms per card, for example chassis-1 G42 (NC) with temp 25 C and power 2.1/4400 W, card-1-1 XMM4 (Act) temp 25 C, card-1-FAN-1 FAN speed 41%. The default scope is the entire network element. For large NEs you can filter by chassis by passing the chassis id, for example status equipment 5; only existing chassis ids are accepted and wildcards are not supported, so you get either all chassis or exactly one. Full syntax: status [[dashboard=]<system | equipment | L0-oxcon | L0-ocm | L1-traffic>] [[filter=]<value>].

Use clear [-f] system [[action=]<value>] [[restart-behavior=]<value>] [type=]<value> [[target=]<value>], in Operational Mode; -f forces the command without confirmation. The type values are factory-reset, full-wipe and inactive. factory-reset resets the system or a particular equipment to factory configuration, stopping target traffic services and removing the respective files and user configurations, which may imply loss of connectivity. target may be the entire system or a chassis/card AID; if no target is given the entire system is cleared. restart-behavior is a standard restart (default) or shutdown, in which case the system does not restart afterwards. Limits: factory-reset does not take effect for 1830 GX G30 Optical Carrier-Cards (OCC2T, OCC2E), it is supported for the G30 controller card (FRCU), and factory-reset with the shutdown option is not supported on L0 cards. For a simple database wipe, use clear database.

Run the time command. It takes no parameters and is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. It prints the system time as a single ISO 8601 style string, for example 2020-06-29T22:29:37+00:00, using the system configured timezone. This is also the command referenced by set-time for reading back the current system time. If you need the individual clock attributes instead, show clock current-time gives the current date and time of the NE and show clock universal-time gives the UTC date and time.

The uptime command displays the system uptime and load average, and takes no parameters; it is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. Sample output is: 21:24:09 up 41 days, 15:56, 1 user, load average: 0.10, 0.35, 0.39. The load average indicates whether multiple tasks are queued on the system (on the card). Whether it is high or low depends on the number of cores the system has, how many CPUs are integrated into the card, and the load average number itself. The rule is that a load average value is considered high when it is greater than the number of CPUs on the card.

Yes, you will lose the management session. The manual-switchover command prompts with: Controller will switchover and connection to the management interface will be lost. Do you want to continue? [y/n]. You must confirm at this prompt to proceed. The syntax is manual-switchover [-f] [resource=]<value> in Operational Mode, where resource is the AID of the object to be manually switched, for example manual-switchover card-1-3 on a 1830 GX G42 chassis, card-1-5 on a G32 chassis, and card-1-12 on a G34c chassis. The -f flag runs the command without the confirmation prompt. For the full procedure, see the 1830 GX Software Management Procedures Guide.

show protection. It takes no parameters and is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode; it displays the node's protection settings container. For the detail beneath it, use show protection-group-<name>, which returns AID, label, protection-type, pg-state, pg-request, pg-control-request, switching-mode, reversion-mode, hold-off-timer, wtr-timer, remaining-wtr, last-switch-trigger, working-pu, protection-pu, reliable-cp, the four switch triggers, switch-failure-reason and alarm-report-control, and show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name> for the individual members.

On protection-group, switching-mode takes unidirectional or bidirectional and defaults to unidirectional. The wait-to-restore timer is wtr-timer: it is the trigger clearance soaking time before reverting to the working protection unit, measured and set in 1-second steps, with a range of 60..720 seconds and a default of 300. It only applies in revertive mode, and reversion-mode (revertive, non-revertive) defaults to non-revertive, so you must set revertive for the WTR timer to have effect. remaining-wtr is a read-only counter in the range 0..720 seconds showing the time left. The separate hold-off-timer, the switching trigger soaking time before switching, is set in 1-millisecond steps with range 0..10000 ms and default 0.

Use the protection-switch operating command in Operational Mode: protection-switch [-f] [operation-type=]<value> [switch-target=]<value> [protection-group=]<value>. operation-type takes force, lockout, manual or release; switch-target names the target of the switch and is not needed for the release and lockout operations. Example: protection-switch protection-group-test operation-type=force switch-target=protection. Equivalently, the protection-group pg-request attribute manages the protection switching action and accepts clear, manual-to-working, manual-to-protection, forced-to-working, forced-to-protection, protection-lockout and exercise (exercise applies only to bidirectional SNCP), with default clear. If the switch does not take, read switch-failure-reason and pg-state on the group.

Run show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name> and read the state attribute, whose values are active, standby, available and unknown; active is the member currently carrying traffic. The companion role attribute reports whether that unit is the working or the protection unit. The command also returns AID, transport-entity, label and alarm-report-control (allowed, inhibited; default inhibited), and is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. At group level, show protection-group-<name> pg-state and last-switch-trigger tell you why the traffic is where it is, and working-pu and protection-pu name the two members.

Use clear [-f] alarm [alarm-type=]<value> [[resource=]<value>[,<value>]*] in Operational Mode; -f forces the command without confirmation. Example: clear alarm DBRESTOREFAIL. Most alarms have both automatic raise and automatic clear criteria; only a very small subset lack a clear criterion and require the user to acknowledge and clear them manually. To find which ones qualify, list the alarm-inventory entries that have can-be-cleared-by-user = true, with show alarm-inventory can-be-cleared-by-user=true. This mechanism applies only to system alarms that are not associated with any particular resource, that is, system wide or global alarms. To acknowledge rather than clear, use set-alarm-state.

That is governed by the system-wide arc-behavior switch on alarm-control: set alarm-control arc-behavior <leave-alarms|clear-alarms>, available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. leave-alarms, which is the default, means that when ARC is set to inhibit the current alarms are left in a raised mode, so they stay up. clear-alarms means that when ARC is set to inhibit the current alarms are cleared. The other attribute on this object is alarm-soaking-behavior, with values automatic (default, soaking time as defined in the FM profile) and no-soak (certain alarms specified in the FM profile have no soaking time); the OSC LOF alarm instead uses the per-facility lof-soak-timer setting on the PBAx card. Read the settings back with show alarm-control.

The alarm-inventory holds the static information for every possible alarm type in the system. Query it with show alarm-inventory-<alarm-type> [resource-type] [alarm-category] [alarm-type-description] [corrective-action] [default-severity] [service-affecting], for example show alarm-inventory-TIM or show alarm-inventory-MSIM. alarm-type-description (string 0..128) explains what the code means and corrective-action (string 0..256) is the system provided information on how to correct the situation that triggered it. alarm-category is one of communication, facility, equipment, environmental, processing-error, software, quality-of-service or security. default-severity lists the possible defaults (critical, major, minor, warning, not-reported, event), which can differ per resource-type, and service-affecting is indeterminate, sa, nsa or sa-nsa.

Yes, that is exactly what alarm-severity-entry is for: it configures the severity of one particular alarm. Use set alarm-severity-entry-<resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> severity <value>, in Operational Mode or Candidate Configuration Mode. resource-type is the card or entity type (for example CHM1R, FAN, 1830 GX G31), alarm-type is the abbreviated code (for example ADMIN-LOCK, BERSD), direction is na, ingress or egress, and location is na, near-end or far-end. severity accepts critical, event, major, minor, not-reported or warning. Examples: set alarm-severity-entry-OTU2/TIM/ingress/near-end severity minor, and set alarm-severity-entry-tom/EQPTCOMFAIL severity major. Press ? after the command to list available entities; show alarm-severity-entry displays all entries and their service-affecting value. The object is system managed and cannot be manually deleted.

alarm-severity-profile sets the severity for an alarm profile rather than addressing an entry by its full key. Syntax: set alarm-severity-profile <profile-entry> severity <critical|event|major|minor|not-reported|warning>, with show alarm-severity-profile to display; Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. The profile-entry is the profile to be modified, named as an alarm-severity-entry path, for example set alarm-severity-profile alarm-severity-entry-trusted-certificate/CERTIFICATE-EXPIRED severity critical. Press ? after set alarm-severity-profile to list the available profiles. By contrast, alarm-severity-entry is keyed explicitly as <resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> and also exposes the read-only service-affecting attribute. Both objects are system managed and cannot be manually deleted, and both take the same six severity values.

Use show current-alarms [number-of-alarms] [last-changed], available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. number-of-alarms is the count of currently raised alarms, and last-changed is the timestamp of the last change in the current alarm list, covering either a raise or a clear event. Plain show current-alarms shows the list of currently raised alarms. For a severity breakdown alongside the count, the system dashboard from the status command reports it in one line, for example: 13 current alarms (1 critical, 5 major, 2 not-reported, 5 minor).

Look at the conditions with the get-conditions command, in Operational Mode. A condition is an alarm that is not considered current, which happens when the alarm severity is configured as not-reported or not-alarmed, when the alarm is suppressed due to alarm correlation, when it is suppressed due to ARC (alarm reporting control), or when it is suppressed due to AINS. Syntax: get-conditions [[direction=]<value>] [[resource=]<value>] [[resource-type=]<value>] [[alarm-type=]<value>] [[location=]<value>] [[AID=]<value>]. direction takes all, na, ingress or egress and defaults to all; location takes all, na, near-end or far-end and defaults to all; resource, resource-type, alarm-type and AID narrow the result to a specific instance or code.

Use set-alarm-state, an Operational Mode command: set-alarm-state [state=]<value> [[acknowledge-text=]<value>] (all-alarms | [alarm-id-list=]<value>[,<value>]*). The state parameter is mandatory and takes the operator-state values 'none', 'ack' and 'close'. For a batch, either use all-alarms, which sets all currently raised alarms, or alarm-id-list, which accepts from 1 up to 10 alarm-ids (leafref) separated by commas. acknowledge-text is optional and stores a string of length 0..256 in the alarm itself. Setting an alarm to its current state is accepted, with only the text updated. Example: set-alarm-state ack all-alarms acknowledge-text=example, or set-alarm-state ack 28872914984089790,17580406225060810165.

Yes. The statistics command clears event counters for specified objects: clear [-f] statistics [target=]<value>[,<value>]*, in Operational Mode. The target parameter is an instance-identifier naming the objects whose event counter statistics are cleared, and it accepts a comma separated list. Scope is limited: the only supported object type is currently aaa-server, and AAA statistics are supported for TACACS+ servers but not for RADIUS servers. The -f flag forces the command without confirmation, and -h displays help. To clear all AAA servers: clear statistics aaa-server. To clear one server: clear statistics aaa-server-MyServer.

Use show log with the -n and -t flags: show [-n=<number>] [-t] log [<logname> [exclude=<exclude-column> ...]]. So show -n=10 -t log security gives the last 10 security log entries in aligned table form. By default log entries are shown in CSV format with each column named in the header; -t switches to the aligned table display, which is easier to read but can be too wide, in which case remove columns with exclude=<column> after the logname (use <tab> auto-complete to list removable columns). Valid lognames include security, messages, event, user, configuration, cli-command, netconf-command, shell-command, alarm, kernel, apps, linecard and ztp. You can also pipe, e.g. show log security | exclude john | include NETCONF. Note the security log may not be cleared due to system restrictions.

Yes, that is expected: the log-console 'enabled' attribute defaults to false, so console logging is off until you turn it on. Use set log-console [source-facilities <value>] [enabled <value>] and show log-console [source-facilities] [enabled], available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Enable it with: set log-console enabled true. The 'enabled' parameter takes true or false and switches console logging on and off. source-facilities is the list of syslog facilities used in this configuration, chosen from all, authentication, clock-daemon-9, clock-daemon-15, ftp-daemon, kernel, line-printer, local1 through local7, log-alert, log-audit, mail-system, network-news, ntp, security, syslog-internal, system-daemons, user-level and uucp.

Add a log-console-facility-filter, which selects messages by source facility and severity: add log-console-facility-filter-<name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>]. The <name> is a single syslog facility, or 'all' for every facility. severity takes emergency (0), alert (1), critical (2), error (3), warning (4), notice (5), informational (6) or debug (7), and defaults to informational. compare-op takes equals, equals-or-higher or not-equals and defaults to equals-or-higher. Since informational plus equals-or-higher is the default, raise the bar, for example: add log-console-facility-filter-all severity 'critical', which passes only critical, alert and emergency. Use set to change it, show to view severity and compare-op, and delete log-console-facility-filter-<name> to remove it.

It is controlled per log file by two log-file attributes. max-file-size is the maximum file size before rotation in megabytes, a uint8 in the range 1..30, default 30. number-of-files is the maximum number of log files retained, a uint8 in the range 1..20, default 10; when rotating files because max-file-size was reached, the oldest files are discarded if the total number of files exceeds number-of-files. So by default a log keeps 10 files of up to 30 MB, and the ceiling is 20 files of 30 MB. Set them with add log-file-<name> [number-of-files <value>] [max-file-size <value>] ... or set log-file-<name> .... The default system log file cannot be edited or deleted; other local files can be emptied with clear or removed with delete.

Yes. Restrict the file to the authentication facility when you create it: add log-file-<name> source-facilities authentication. source-facilities is the list of syslog facilities used in that configuration and defaults to all; the authentication facility is syslog facility 4, used for authentication/authorization attempt messages. To also bound severity, add a filter under that file: add log-file-facility-filter-<log-file-name>/<log-file-facility-filter-name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>], where the filter name is a single facility or 'all', severity defaults to informational and compare-op defaults to equals-or-higher. Example: add log-file-facility-filter-myauth/authentication severity warning compare-op equals-or-higher. The file name itself is a string of 0...128 characters, without the .log extension.

Configure the collector with add log-server-<name> address <IP address> ... port <value> transport <udp|tls|tcp>. For TLS you must state transport tls explicitly, because the transport default is udp. Unless you say otherwise the port defaults to 514 (range 1..65535) and message-format defaults to rfc5424 (the alternative is rfc3164). Other defaults: enabled true, message-coalescence true, origin manual, source-facilities all, destination-facility-override disabled (else a facility number in range 0..11 or 16..23), sensitive-data none, alarm-report-control allowed. The name is a string of 0...64 characters and address accepts IPv4, IPv6 or a DNS domain name. Example: add log-server-1 address '10.220.225.165' source-facilities local7.

Yes you can filter per collector, but no, the filter cannot widen what is sent. Use add log-server-facility-filter-<log-server-name>/<log-server-facility-filter-name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>]. The filter is based on the log-server's source-facilities leaf-list and can only add a filter to the already configured source facilities, so it narrows rather than extends the set. The filter name identifies a single syslog facility, or all of them if the value is 'all'. severity takes emergency, alert, critical, error, warning, notice, informational or debug, default informational; compare-op takes equals, equals-or-higher or not-equals, default equals-or-higher. Example: add log-server-facility-filter-server184/local2 severity debug. Remove it with the matching delete command.

Use the syslog container's remote-logging-switch: set syslog remote-logging-switch false. It is a flag to enable remote logging; if false, all remote logging destinations are disabled, so your configured log-server entries stay in place and simply stop being used. The default is true. The command runs in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode, and you can check it with show syslog remote-logging-switch. Related syslog attributes are source-address (default localhost), log-file-message-coalescence (default true), log-relay (default false, which disables remote logging from a shelf controller to a node controller), assignment-method (both, manual or dhcp, default both), niap-compliant-logging (default false), privacy-mode (default false), alarm-report-control (default allowed) and label (string 0..256).

The shared-secret of an aaa-server is documented as a string of length 0...128 with default 'sharedkey', but the enforced maximum length is 64 characters: any value longer than 64 characters is denied with an error message. The value is displayed as * when shown. Set it with add aaa-server-<server-name> ... [shared-secret <value>] or set aaa-server-<server-name> [shared-secret <value>], in Operational Mode or Candidate Configuration Mode. For context, the server-name itself is a string of length 1...64, protocol-supported is RADIUS or TACACSPLUS (default RADIUS), server-port defaults to 49, server-port-authentication to 1812 and server-port-accounting to 1813.

No, that is expected behaviour. In show aaa-statistics-<server-name>, the authentication-requests counter displays the number of authentication requests, and for TACACS+ the default authentication protocol includes both PAP and CHAP. The counter tracks each retry and each authentication protocol attempted independently, so authentication requests may increase by 2 for each retry. The command is show aaa-statistics-<server-name> [connection-failures] [authentication-requests] [authentication-rejects] [authorization-requests] [authorization-rejects] [accounting-requests], available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode, and it applies to AAA servers that use the TACACS+ protocol. connection-failures covers failures due to unavailable servers and timeouts.

If you omit action, the ACE defaults to drop; the permitted values are drop, accept and reject. Add rules with add ace-<name>/<sequence-id> [action <value>] [direction <value>] [protocol <value>] [ttl <value>] .... Pre-condition: the ACL must already exist before an ACE can be added, and at least one of source IP, destination IP, L4 ports, TTL or protocol must be provided. Limits: sequence-id ranges 1-100 for AUX and DCN-B interfaces and 1-256 for the DCN-A interface, and multiples of 5 are recommended so rules can be inserted later. A maximum of 16 ACEs can be created on an ACL if both upper-port and lower-port values are specified; attempting a 17th such ACE returns an error. Other defaults: direction input, protocol any, ttl 255, ports 0, logging-action false.

Attach an ACL with add acl-<name> type <value> interface <value> [admin-state <value>]. The available interfaces are 1-AUX-1, 1-AUX-2, DCN, DCN-B, DCN-2 and DCN-2-B; use add acl-name interface ? to list them. An ACL can be added on the DCN-B interface when the DCN is operating in active-active configuration. Yes, IPv6 is handled: the type parameter indicates the top-level type of ACL, that is which fields of the associated IPv4 or IPv6 header the ACL matches on, and takes IPv4 or IPv6 with no default. The ACL name is a string of 0...30 characters, and admin-state takes lock, maintenance or unlock, defaulting to unlock. Example: add acl-AuxV4traffic interface 1-AUX-2 type ipv4. Each ACL can hold one or more ACEs.

Yes: show access-control-list. It is a show-only command used to display the access control list, with no parameters, and it is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For per-ACL detail use show acl-<name> [admin-state] [oper-state] [avail-state] [type] [interface], and for the individual entries use show ace-<name>/<sequence-id> [label] [direction] [logging-action] [source-ip-address] [source-lower-port] [source-upper-port] [destination-ip-address] [destination-lower-port] [destination-upper-port] [ttl] [action] [protocol].

Add an access-rule with action deny under an access-rule-list bound to that group: add access-rule-<access-rule-list-name>/<access-rule-name> action <value> [sequence-id <value>] [module-name <value>] [path <value>] [attribute <value>] [attribute-value <value>] [operation <value>] [description <value>]. action is mandatory and takes permit or deny. path is the target object, an XPath of a YANG data node, notification, RPC or descendant, or an external command, max 255 characters, default '*'. operation is a bits value over create, read, update, delete and execute, default '*', so to block writes use operation 'create update delete'. Example: add access-rule-1/rule path /ne/equipment/card operation create action deny. Bind the list to the group with add access-rule-list-<name> user-group <group>. The system supports a maximum of 500 access-rules across all access-rule-lists.

Ordering is by sequence-id: the access-rule-list is processed in order given by sequence-id, and lower number ids are processed first, so the lowest sequence-id wins. sequence-id is a uint16 and can be changed over the lifetime of the list to re-sort entries; if not provided it is set to the currently used latest id plus 1, placing the entry at the end of the list. The same sequence-id semantics apply to individual access-rules inside a list. To say which groups a list applies to, use the user-group parameter: add access-rule-list-<name> [user-group <value>] [sequence-id <value>] [description <value>]. user-group is a leaf-list of user-group names, defaulting to '*' which matches all existing user-groups, and a maximum of 20 user-groups can be referenced. Example: add access-rule-list-A user-group XY. description is a string of 0..256 characters.

Despite the generic name, auth-key is OSPFv3 IPsec specific: the key parameter is the pre-shared key for OSPFv3 IPsec integrity protection. The AID is fully OSPF-scoped: add auth-key-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id>/<ospf-if-name>/<spi> key <value> [type <value>], where instance-id is the OSPF instance ID (number, range 0..255), ospf-area-id is the OSPF Router Area ID (string), ospf-if-name references the interface in the OSPF area (string), and spi is a unique security parameter index for the SA (number, range 256..4294967295). key is a string of length 8..128, and type indicates whether the integrity key is ASCII or hexadecimal encoded, taking ascii or hex. Available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: add auth-key-1/0.0.0.0/DCN/256 key abcdefgh12345678.

Set the global authorization mode to rules-only and make the write fallback deny: set authorization mode rules-only, then set authorization write-default deny. mode selects which authorization rules are used and takes static-only (only system defined static rules), static+rules (both user and system defined rules, user rules checked first with system rules as fallback) or rules-only (only user defined access-rules, with the global defaults used when no rule matches); the default is static+rules. read-default, write-default and exec-default are only configurable when mode = rules-only, take permit or deny, and default to permit, deny and permit respectively. Read covers get/show and receiving notifications, write covers create/update/delete, exec covers RPC invocation. show authorization also reports denied-operations, denied-data-writes and denied-notifications since the last restart.

A user changes their own password with the password command: password [old-password=<old-password>] [new-password=<new-password>], in Operational mode. Both the current and the new password must be provided, and this is supported only for local users. Run it bare to be prompted interactively, in which case the input is not echoed and the new password must be typed twice; Ctrl+C cancels. Inline form, usable in scripts: password old-password=Infinera4u! new-password=Infinera4us!, where " and ' must be escaped with backslash and #?|; must be quoted. A password may contain up to 200 characters. An administrator resets someone else's password with set user-<username> force-password-change true, which forces that user to change their password on next login; force-password-change defaults to false.

show security. It is the command used to display the top level security container, takes no parameters, and is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: show security, which views all of the system's security containers. For the policy flags underneath it, use show security-policies [secure-mode] [strict-password-check] [minimum-password-length] [ssh-authentication-method] [default-user-group] [enforce-password-history-check] [password-history-size] [aaa-authentication-method] [aaa-authorization-method] and the remaining SSH, TLS and certificate revocation attributes.

minimum-password-length is the configurable minimum length for user passwords, a number in range 1..200 with a default of 8; it is verified whenever a password is changed. History: enforce-password-history-check defaults to true and ensures a new password cannot match any of the previous 5 passwords for that user; password-history-size is the number of passwords stored for reuse checking, range 1..200, default 5. Both only affect newly defined passwords once enabled. strict-password-check also defaults to true and enforces minimum length 8 plus at least one lower case letter, one upper case letter, one number and one symbol, and forbids the user name being part of the password; if disabled, only a minimum length of 1 character applies. Set these with set security-policies minimum-password-length <n> password-history-size <n>.

Both thresholds are per-user attributes of the user command. max-invalid-login is the maximum number of consecutive invalid login attempts before an account is suspended (locked out): a number in range 0-255, default 5. suspension-time is the duration of UID suspension following those consecutive invalid login attempts, in minutes, range 0 - 1440, default 5. Set them with add user-<user-name> ... [max-invalid-login <value>] [suspension-time <value>] or set user-<user-name> .... show user-<user-name> also reports failed-logins, the number of previous failed logins, which resets to zero upon a successful login, and user-status, where the value 'lockout' means the account is locked out due to unsuccessful login attempts. Lockout can also be turned off globally through the security-policies disable-user-lockout parameter.

user-data is a display-only command: show user-data. It shows the user-data container and takes no parameters at all. It is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. There is no add, set or delete form. For per-user attributes use show user-<user-name> [password] [password-hashed] [user-group] [display-name] [max-invalid-login] [suspension-time] [timeout] [password-aging-interval] [password-expiration-date] [enabled] [user-status] [force-password-change] [max-sessions] [last-login-date] [failed-logins] [user-aaa-type] [alarm-report-control] [label], and for groups use show user-group-<name> [description].

Use add user-group-<name> [description <value>], in Operational mode or Candidate Configuration mode. The group name is a string of 1...64 characters and description is a long description of the user group, a string of 1...128 characters; neither has a default. Each user is associated with a list of groups and derives its permissions from them, so you then attach the group through the user's user-group attribute, which accepts the built-ins EA, MA, NA, NE, PR, SA, TT and user-defined groups. Example: add user-group-XY. Modify with set user-group-<name> description <value>, view with show user-group-<name> [description] or show user-group for all of them, and remove with delete user-group-XY. The predefined groups are EA Encryption Administrator, MA Monitoring Access, NA Network Administrator, NE Network Engineer, PR Provisioning, SA Security Administrator and TT Turn-up and Test.

Add/Drop Groups are created with 'add adg-<adg-number>'; adg-number is an integer in the range [1..110], so a node can hold up to 110 ADGs (this matches max-adgs = 110 from 'show oadm-capabilities'). Duplication is governed by the read-only 'wavelength-duplication' attribute, shown with 'show adg-<adg-number> wavelength-duplication'. Its values are 'one-per-adg' (default: no duplication of frequencies in the ADG) and 'one-per-degree' (CDC: duplication of frequencies allowed in the ADG, but only one at the Degree). Only CDCs allow more than one instance of the same wavelength on the ADG. Other ADG attributes are 'label' (string 0..256), read-only 'max-add-drop-ports', and 'bands-supported' (default standardC-band).

Gain is requested with 'set amplifier-<name> gain-target <value>', range 0..40 dB, default 0.0; it applies only in manual control mode. 'control-mode' is auto-max-pw (default, auto mode targeting maximum output power) or manual; in auto mode use 'gain-adjustment' [-20.00..20.00], default 0, to offset the automatically calculated gain (supported only on amplifiers with function 'pa' or 'inline'). 'gain-operating' shows the actually configured gain (0..40 dB). Tilt is controlled by 'tilt-control-mode': auto (default, system implicitly controls tilt per configured fiber parameters), auto-planned (per planning tool parameters), or manual (user controls tilt). So yes, the system controls tilt by itself unless you set manual; when amplifier function is 'add' or 'drop' the only option is manual. 'tilt-target' applies in manual mode and 'tilt-adjustment' offsets auto/auto-planned, both [-5..5] dB, default 0 dB; 'tilt-actual' is the measured value.

Use 'set amplifier-raman-<name> target-raman-gain <value>'. The permitted range is [0, 5..30dB] with default 0dB. It is configurable only when 'control-mode' is different from auto; in auto control-mode the parameter is ignored. The three control-mode values are auto (default: configure only span attributes, gain is automatically controlled), auto-planned (configure target Raman gain plus span attributes) and manual (basic manual configuration, where even the target pump powers must be configured). Pump count comes from the read-only 'number-of-pumps' attribute: 'show amplifier-raman-<name> number-of-pumps'. It reports the number of pumps for the required-equipped card, either 4 or 2, and that value dictates how many pump-power objects the system exposes. Related read-outs are total-pump-power [-99..99 dBm], actual-raman-signal-gain and actual-raman-osc-gain.

Switch it on with 'set ase-idler-service-<name> ase-idler-enable enabled' (for example 'set ase-idler-service-1-8 ase-idler-enable enabled'); ase-idler-enable can also be given on 'add ase-idler-service-<name>'. Values are enabled and disabled, default disabled. Enabled means ASE idler signal filling on the unused and nmc-failed portions of the band spectrum is enabled. To check whether it actually came up, read the system-reported 'ase-idler-state' with 'show ase-idler-service-<name> ase-idler-state': ase-enabled (filling is complete on the band spectrum), ase-partially-enabled (filling is incomplete), ase-faulted (ASE idler signal is faulted), or ase-disabled (default, signal completely removed from the band spectrum). 'oper-state' (enabled/disabled) and 'avail-state' are also shown. The 'function' attribute is 'idler'.

Set it with 'set ase-idler-source-<name> target-output-power <value>'. The range is (-3.00..20.50) dBm with a default of 13; it is the ASE pump output power required when manually configured. The pump is not on by default: 'pump-enable' has values enabled and disabled with default disabled, so you must explicitly enable it. A combined example is 'set ase-idler-source-1-3.1-ase pump-enable enabled target-output-power 15.00'. To verify, read the system-reported 'pump-state' (enabled/disabled, default disabled) with 'show ase-idler-source-<name> pump-state'. The object's 'function' is ase-idler-source; other settable attributes are admin-state (lock/unlock/maintenance, default unlock), label and alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default allowed).

Use the operational-mode 'calibrate' command: 'calibrate [type=]<value> [trigger=]<value> [entity=]<value>'. The only supported 'type' is 'raman', which triggers calibration on raman cards. 'trigger' takes 'start' (starts the Raman gain calibration for the OTS span) or 'stop' (stops the Raman gain calibration for the OTS span). 'entity' selects the entity to be calibrated, and its type depends on the type parameter; for raman calibration the entity may be an OTS-R entity, given as an instance-identifier. To start: 'calibrate raman start ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line'. To stop: 'calibrate raman stop ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line'. None of the three parameters has a default. Access mode is Operational Mode only.

Degrees are created with 'add degree-<degree-number>'; degree-number is an integer in the range [1..20] and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees, so a node supports up to 20 degrees (matching max-degrees = 20 from 'show oadm-capabilities'). Spectral granularity is read back with 'show degree-<degree-number>': 'slot-width-granularity' is the width of a slot with a default of 6250 (value in MHz), and 'center-freq-granularity' is the granularity of allowed center frequencies, default 3125 MHz, computed from a base frequency of 193.1 THz (G.694.1). Media channels are built from slots: 'min-slots' defaults to 8 and 'max-slots' to 32, min-slots must be less than or equal to max-slots. Also shown are is-foadm, wss-less and bands-supported (default standardC-band).

On a multi-rail ILA node the system pairs directions to the two line ports of each ILAx card. Direction n and direction n+1 are automatically assigned by the system to the DWDM Line1 and DWDM Line2 ports of the #n C2ILASGH/D2ILASGM card created, where index n is an odd integer with a value between 1 and 15. DWDM Line1 is always assigned an odd index value and DWDM Line2 always an even index value. The direction index range is [1..16] (1 and 2 are used when migrating from R6.x). The system sets 'direction-number' from the configured 'direction-port': 1 for dwdm-line1, 2 for dwdm-line2. So an odd index should carry port-<shelf>-<slot>-dwdm-line1 and an even index port-<shelf>-<slot>-dwdm-line2, and the same dwdm-line* port instance of an ILAx can only be selected once per NE. 'direction-card' is filled in autonomously from the port. Syntax: 'add direction-<index> direction-port <value> [label <value>]'; 'delete -f' forces deletion without confirmation.

With 'add dsc-<name>' or 'set dsc-<name>' you can configure only three attributes: 'label' (string 0..256), 'admin-state' (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock) and 'alarm-report-control' (allowed or inhibited; default allowed). Everything else is show-only: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled), avail-state and managed-by. The 'managed-by' attribute describes whether this facility was system created or not; values are 'system' and 'user' with default 'system'. It matters operationally because only user-created facilities can be user deleted, so a dsc showing managed-by system cannot be removed with 'delete dsc-<name>'. Access mode is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

On dsc-group you set four Q-related attributes, available on both 'add dsc-group-<name>' and 'set dsc-group-<name>'. Pre-FEC: 'pre-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold' raises the PRE-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE alarm, decimal64 with 3 fraction digits, range 0|5.600..9.600 dB, where 0 disables threshold crossing alarming and the specific sub-range is per carrier use-case; its 'pre-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis' is decimal64 with 1 fraction digit, range 0.1..1.0 dB, default 0.5. Post-FEC: 'post-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold' raises POST-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE, 1 fraction digit, range 12.5..18.0 dB, default 18; 'post-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis' range 0.1..1.0 dB, default 0.5. Related is 'dgd-high-threshold' for the DGD-OORH alarm, uint16 range 25..400 ps, default 100.

Use the gadt command, which retrieves golden carrier application information: 'show gadt [<application-description-H|application-description-P|application-description-S|application-description-U>]'. Each of the four parameters is a detailed description of an application ID and is a string with no default. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For example, 'show gadt application-description-H' returns application-description 'Subsea modes using Uniform and Hybrid modulation'. Run 'show gadt' with no argument to see all four. The application ID letter also appears as the 'application' field in golden carrier mode output from gcmt and golden-carrier-mode.

The gapt command lists the golden advanced parameters from the Golden Advanced Parameters Table (GAPT). Syntax is 'show gapt-<card-type> [version] [applicable-resource-type]', so it is scoped per card type: card-type is a string naming the card, 'version' is the table version (string, length 0..5) and 'applicable-resource-type' names the managed resource type(s) applicable for that advanced parameter. None have defaults. A plain 'show gapt' lists the tables per card, for example gapt-CHM6 version 1.8, gapt-CHM7 version 3.0, gapt-CHM7T. Scoping to one card, 'show gapt-chm7', lists that card's entries such as golden-advanced-parameter-CHM7/BOASetting, /NLC, /RxCDMode, /TxSignalBWControl, along with version '3.0'. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use the gcmt command, which retrieves information about the golden carrier mode: 'show gcmt [<card-type>] [version]', where the object parameter is the golden carrier modes string and version is the table version. For a specific mode, name it directly: 'show gcmt golden-carrier-mode-800M.95P'. The output row is keyed by card type, for example golden-carrier-mode-CHM6/800M.95P, and reports capacity (Gbps) 800, client-mode ethernet-otn, baud-rate (GBaud) 95.2965203, application P, compatibility-id 6, and status supported. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For the full per-mode attribute set use 'show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode>'.

Read the 'status' attribute, which describes the carrier mode release status: 'show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode> status'. Its values are supported, candidate, experimental, deprecated and diagnostic, with no default. So a mode reporting 'supported' is fully supported, while 'experimental' (or 'candidate'/'diagnostic') is not. The same status column appears in gcmt output, for example 'show gcmt golden-carrier-mode-800M.95P' returning status 'supported'. The carrier-mode key is a string (1..15) formatted <Capacity><ClientMode>.<Baud Rate><Application ID>, such as 600E.84P, 100X.73U or 325M.66P. Related attributes are 'supported-subtypes' (string 0..32, maximum 20 elements) and 'candidate-subtypes' (string 0..16, maximum 10 elements), which name the subtypes for which the mode has candidate status.

The 'l0-capabilities' command shows the capabilities details related with the node's Layer 0 functions. The syntax is simply 'show l0-capabilities'; it takes no parameters at all. Access mode is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. For the OADM-specific limits use the companion command 'show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs]', which reports max-degrees 20 and max-adgs 110.

A Media Channel is carved out with 'add mc-<name> parent-oms <value> lower-frequency <value> upper-frequency <value> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [auto-delete <value>]'. The three mandatory inputs are parent-oms, lower-frequency and upper-frequency. parent-oms is an instance-identifier set only upon MC creation, and its referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree (it cannot be in an ADG). lower-frequency and upper-frequency are values in MHz. The system derives 'center-frequency' and 'slot-width' (upper-frequency minus lower-frequency), both read-only in MHz. Example: 'add mc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 parent-oms 1-3.1-dwdm-line lower-frequency 192225000 upper-frequency 192300000'. 'auto-delete' defaults to disabled and is allowed to be enabled only on RD66TM sleds (l0-mode-op=hsc-ols); it is always disabled if l0-mode-op is standard or slte.

The Media Channel Filler is read only. The mc-f command supports only 'show mc-f-<name> [supporting-facilities] [supported-facilities] [supporting-card] [supporting-port] [AID] [lower-frequency] [upper-frequency] [slot-width]' with no add, set or delete form, and every parameter is marked as used in 'show' only. lower-frequency and upper-frequency are the lower and upper frequency of the MC Filler in MHz units, and slot-width is calculated by the system as upper-frequency minus lower-frequency, also in MHz units; none of them have defaults. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. By contrast the Network Media Channel Filler command nmc-f does allow 'set nmc-f-<name> [admin-state] [alarm-report-control]'.

Up to four cards go into one ADG. 'add modules-adg-<adg-number>/<index> supported-card <value> [ocm-monitoring <value>]' takes adg-number in the range [1..110] and index in the range [1..4]. The card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). Example: 'add modules-adg-1/1 supported-card card-1-6'. Channel monitoring is on by default: 'ocm-monitoring' has values true and false with a default of true. It is set upon creation and cannot be changed after supported-card has been assigned, but it can optionally be configured to false for OMD cards directly connected to PAx/BAX or C2ILASGH degrees, for example FOADM nodes. Access mode is Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode; user access privilege level is Network Administrator or Network Engineer.

Associate a card with a degree using 'add modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card <value>'. degree-number is a number in the range [1..20] and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees. The index is fixed at 1: the card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). 'supported-card' is an instance identifier for the card or subcard that belongs to the degree; in R6.0 the card must be RD09SM or RD20TM. Example: 'add modules-degree-1/1 supported-card card-1-1'. You can also 'set modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card <value>', 'show' it, or 'delete modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index>'. Access mode is Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode; user access privilege level is Network Administrator or Network Engineer.

Use 'show monitored-channel-<name>/<frequency> monitored-optical-power'. The name corresponds to the (WS04S) card name with the suffix -1 or -2, for ocm1-in or ocm2-in respectively, and frequency is the nominal center frequency of the carrier (channel) in MHz as a uint32. Example: 'show monitored-channel-1-1.2-ocm1-in/195987500 monitored-optical-power'; omit the attribute name to see all attributes of that channel. 'monitored-optical-power' is the measured power for the corresponding carrier in dBm, decimal64 in the range (-99.00..99.00) with default -99, where -99.00 means no power. The other attribute is 'monitored-width', the carrier width configured at the NMC within the oxcon source/destination in MHz (uint32, default 0). The command is show-only, in Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode.

On 'add nmc-<name> parent-facility <value> center-frequency <value> ...' the nominal center-frequency takes values in the range [190650000..196700000] MHz and has no default; it is only settable at creation. 'width' is the Network Media Channel frequency width in MHz, values in the range [15000..200000] MHz with a default of 35000. The user must configure the 3 dB signal bandwidth, and the value in GHz must be equivalent to the baud rate (GBd) configured on the connected transponder line interface line port. 'parent-facility' can be either a Media Channel or an OMS and is only set upon creation, and the referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree (cannot be in an ADG). Example: 'add nmc-cdc-1-4_192800000-34000 center-frequency 192800000 width 34000 parent-facility oms-1-4-ad1'.

The Network Media Channel Filler occupies 75000 MHz by default: 'alloc-bandwidth', the allocated bandwidth of the NMC Filler, is a value in MHz units with a default of 75000. The actual occupancy is reported separately by 'actual-bandwidth' (MHz units, default 0), alongside alloc-lower-frequency, alloc-upper-frequency, actual-lower-frequency and actual-upper-frequency. It is monitored: 'monitoring-state' indicates whether the NMC is intended to be in use, values enabled and disabled, and because this is a system created attribute it is enabled by default. Read them with 'show nmc-f-<name>', for example 'show nmc-f-1-3-dwdm-line-58'. Only 'admin-state' (lock/unlock/maintenance, default unlock) and 'alarm-report-control' (allowed/inhibited, default allowed) are settable via 'set nmc-f-<name>'.

Run 'show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs]'. 'max-degrees' is the maximum number of degrees, reported as 20 (uint8), and is 0 if not supported; degrees are only supported in OADM node types, and the maximum degrees for ILA node-type is 0 by convention since an ILA has only 2 directions, fixedly (this is not shown in supported capabilities). Note that the maximum number of Degrees is not necessarily the deployment supported configurations, but the maximum number of a working degree-number. 'max-adgs' is the maximum number of Add/Drop Groups, reported as 110 (uint8), 0 if not supported, and ADGs are only supported in OADM node types. Sample output: max-degrees 20, max-adgs 110. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Loopbacks are set with 'set oc-<name> loopback <value>' where the values are facility, terminal and none, default none; it is useful to debug on the fiber connection. A companion attribute 'loopback-mode' indicates the loopback action for facility or terminal, values facility and terminal, no default. Test patterns are set with 'test-signal-type', whose values are none, enumeration, PRBS31Q, PRBS13Q, scrambled-idles, PRBS9 and PRBS31, default none. 'test-signal-direction' supports only 'ingress' (default ingress), and 'test-signal-monitoring' (true/false, default false) monitors the incoming test signals for diagnostics. Example: 'set oc-1-5-T9.1 test-signal-monitoring false'. Access mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

In ILA nodes the OCHm represents the signaled optical channel from OSC, detected at the ILA OMS by using the OSC information. That has a direct consequence: when either the OMS 'monitoring-mode' is 'not-monitored' (as configured by the user), or there is no OSC messaging information, the list of OCHm facilities in the NE will be empty. Read the facilities with 'show ochm' or 'show ochm-<name>'; 'direction' is ingress or egress but currently only egress is supported (default egress). 'power-actual' is the currently received power in dBm, where -99 dBm means the power is not yet measured (measurement is performed by the OCM at the DGE2 card) or no power detected / no appropriate fiber-connection; for egress it is calibrated at the DWDM Line port output, at the same reference point where the target power is defined. 'target-actual-power' (-99.00..99.00 dBm) and 'attenuation-actual' (0..55 dB) apply to HSC OLS nodes. Settable: label, admin-state, alarm-report-control.

Use the ocm-channel facility: show ocm-channel-<name>/<lower-frequency>/<upper-frequency> [opm-pwr] [connected]. It lists the detected carriers within the configured OXcon(s). The instance is keyed by name (String, length 0..64) plus lower-frequency and upper-frequency (uint32), which bound the corresponding spectrum power (OPM-pwr) point. Two reported values: opm-pwr, the Optical Parameter Monitor power in dBm, decimal64 in range -99.00..99.00 with default -99; and connected, which yields true if the channel is configured, that is, involved in an oxcon, with default false. ocm-channel is show-only and is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Yes. On ocm-mp the attribute ocm-enable, which enables regular power monitoring, takes enabled or disabled and its default is enabled. Change it with set ocm-mp-<name> ocm-enable disabled (or enabled); the other settable attributes are label (String 0..256) and admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock). Separately, monitoring-state is a read-only indicator: the system reports enabled when an OMS reference exists, otherwise disabled. Also read-only: monitored-port (default not-applicable, can differ from supporting-port on a non-integrated OCM), ad-direction (only ingress), oper-state (default disabled) and managed-by (system). Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode.

The ocm-ptp facility is available for WS04S cards within a CD-AD ADG and provides dedicated OCM monitoring. It is not on out of the box: ocm-enable (enabled, disabled) defaults to disabled, so you must turn it on, for example set ocm-ptp-1-1.2-ocm1-in ocm-enable enabled. Read-only monitoring-state also defaults to disabled and is reported enabled only when complete connectivity at the AD is established and OCM measurement is possible. Other show attributes: ad-direction (egress or ingress, default ingress), adg-number (uint8, range 0..110, default 0), and last-measurement, the last OCM scan date and time, default never. Settable: label, admin-state (default unlock), ocm-enable.

On oms the grid-mode attribute defaults to flexible, which allows creating and deleting MCs of different widths. The other choices are fixed-50G-96ch, fixed-100G-48ch, fixed-75G-64ch, fixed-75G-64ch-oif, fixed-50G-7100 (50 GHz, 88 channels, set automatically when osc-compatibility is osc-7100) and fixed-150G-40ch. Default spectral limits are lower-frequency 191300000 and upper-frequency 196150000 MHz (standardC-band). monitoring-mode selects how the section is monitored: not-monitored (non-intrusive, no OCM/DGE), intrusive (TTP), non-intrusive (CTP, operates with OCM), dge-fixed-attenuation, ila-with-equalization (DGE plus OCM), integrated-equalization. Default is intrusive for all node types except ILA, not-monitored for ILA, integrated-equalization for hyperscale ILA. It is only exposed for an OMS on a port belonging to a degree, or on node-type ILA.

set ops-<name> accepts label, admin-state, alarm-report-control, input-psd-profile, role and port-expansion. input-psd-profile is the nominal expected tributary channel power density in dBm/12.5GHz, decimal64 range -30..-6, default -6. role selects the OPS role: tributary (single add/drop to a local or remote transponder), multi-carrier (multiple carriers on the underlying filter port), general-purpose (other cases, such as express cross-connection to another filter), ase-input (only on specific RD ports, in SLTE l0-mode-op) and active-multi-carrier (port has active control); the default is general-purpose. port-expansion is no or y-cable, default no, intended for Y-cable expansion. supported-roles is read-only and exposes which roles the card and card-mode allow. Example: set ops-1-6-ad1 role tributary.

On optical-carrier, frequency is the center frequency in MHz with the generic range 0 | 191275000..196125000 (0 means not configured); the usable range depends on module and pluggable, for example CHM7 and CHM7X 190625000-196725000 MHz in 50 MHz steps, CHM6 191333000-196117000 MHz in 50 MHz steps, CHM2TX 191292500-196137500 MHz in 1 MHz steps, and TOM-400G-C-DWDM on CHM1R 191275000-196125000 MHz with fine tune. tx-power has the generic range -55.0..55.00 dBm and is adjustable in 0.5 dBm steps, again module dependent: CHM2TX -6 to 0 (default 0), CHM7/CHM7X -10 to 0 (default -2), UTM2 -15 to 0 (default -6.0); some pluggables are not configurable. Yes, you can trim: frequency-offset is int16 in range -6000..6000 MHz, default 0, used for bright tuning; once set, the frequency changes slowly over 1-10 s without affecting service.

Yes, use propagate-shutdown on optical-carrier: set optical-carrier-<name> propagate-shutdown enabled. When set, the transmit laser is shut down if the whole service of that direction has signal failure; the function is mainly used at a regeneration node to propagate signal failure as LOS. Values are enabled and disabled, and the default is disabled. Pair it with propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer, the hold off time of propagate shutdown, a number in the range 0..2000 milliseconds with default 0. Restriction: neither propagate-shutdown nor propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer is configurable on the SPN2 or SPN2C card. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Very little. The optical-channel command supports only edit and show, and set optical-channel-<name> accepts just two attributes: label, a user defined string of length 0..256, and admin-state, which takes lock, unlock or maintenance and defaults to unlock. Example: set optical-channel-channel1 admin-state unlock. Everything else on the object is read-only via show optical-channel-<name>: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID (String 1..64), oper-state (enabled or disabled, default disabled), avail-state, and managed-by (system or user, default system; only user-created facilities can be user deleted). Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Read laser-state with show optical-ptp-<name> laser-state. It reports the emitting pump (for example booster) laser state as enabled or disabled, default disabled, and is only of relevance for DWDM line ports; on RD amplifiers it reflects the source (Tx) pump, on Raman modules the pump laser. Yes, you can declare fixed pad: fix-rx-attenuation is a fixed attenuator before port Rx, decimal64 with 2 fraction digits in range 0..30 dB, default 0, where 0 dB means no fixed attenuator. Example: set -f optical-ptp-1-6-dwdm fix-rx-attenuation 10. The companion fix-tx-attenuation has the same range and default but is only visible when ops.port-expansion=y-cable is configured. Measured levels are power-actual-rx and power-actual-tx, -99.00..99.00 dBm, default -99 dBm.

The Signal Fail decision uses working-los-threshold and protection-los-threshold on optical-switch. Both are configurable optical power in the range -55.0 to 0 dBm and both default to -23 dBm, so by default the path is declared failed below -23 dBm. Signal Degrade uses working-switch-threshold and protection-switch-threshold, same -55.0 to 0 dBm range, default -18 dBm, and SD-based switching only acts when switch-threshold-enable is enabled (default disabled). facility-los-threshold covers the facility port, range -55 to 15 dBm, default -30.0 dBm. Hysteresis: los-threshold-hysteresis default 3 dB and switch-threshold-hysteresis default 2 dB, each decimal64 in range 0.5 to 5.0 dB in 0.1 dB steps, with 1 dB recommended for MCHP and OMSP deployments.

set osc-<name> accepts label, admin-state, alarm-report-control, l0-comm-interface-type, osc-control, target-output-power, tx-power-adjustment, voa-attenuation-target-rx and lof-soak-timer. osc-control is auto or manual, default auto; auto control exists from R6.0.1 and HSC OLS nodes support auto only. target-output-power is the OSC Tx power at the DWDM line port output: na or -2.5..4.5 dBm, default na. tx-power-adjustment trims the automatically calculated target: na or -6..6 dB, default 0. voa-attenuation-target-rx is the Rx VOA target for manual control, 0..30 dB, default 10. l0-comm-interface-type is ipv4 or ipv6 (ipv4 for standard OLS, ipv6 for SLTE and HSC OLS). lof-soak-timer is short (about 3 ms) or long (adds 18,400 OC-3 frames, about 2300 ms), default short, visible only for the PBAx card. Read-only include osc-mode, osc-wavelength, voa-attenuation-actual-rx, power-actual-rx/tx.

Read otdr-state with show otdr-<name> otdr-state. It indicates the current status of the OTDR and a status change triggers a change notification. Values are not-available (status is not available), idle, measuring (measurement ongoing), finished (measurement completed) and fail (measurement failed); the default is not-available. Supporting read-only attributes: otdr-measurement-time, the time remaining in the running measurement (default 0); otdr-error, the error message produced when the measurement ends with error; otdr-laser-state (not-available, enabled, disabled); otdr-measurement-port, where 0 means the card is not measuring any port; otdr-measurement-direction (not-available, tx, rx); and otdr-ongoing-measurement-profile (none, short, medium, long, raman-precheck1, raman-precheck2, raman-precheck3).

On otdr-ptp you can add or set: otdr-range, the distance range, auto or 0...300.0 km, default auto, recommended to be the actual fiber length plus 10 percent; from R9.1, if the OTS can be traced from the fiber connection between the ILA/ROADM card and OTDR8OFP2, auto is derived from OTS fiber-length-tx/rx with 10 percent margin rounded up to the nearest 10 km. otdr-resolution is the data sampling resolution, auto or 0.4...100.0, default auto. otdr-pulse-width is auto or 10...20,000 ns. otdr-measurement-speed is fast (about 10 s), medium (15 s), slow (1 min), precision (3-5 min), high-precision (5-7 min) or auto, default auto. otdr-ior is auto or 1.0...2.0. peak-power is auto or 5...14.5. launching-fiber-length is 0...50 m, default 0, and auto is not supported. Also otdr-fiber-type and otdr-direction-mode (default counter-prop-in-service).

On the ots facility. Fibre type: fiber-type-tx and fiber-type-rx, both defaulting to SSMF, with choices including AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS, VistaCor (fiber-type-rx also allows not-applicable, auto and not-configured). Length: fiber-length-tx and fiber-length-rx, auto or 0..500.0 km, default auto, needed for tilt control and for Raman backward pumping. Loss: span-loss-transmit 0..80 dB and span-loss-receive 0..80 or 99 dB, both default 0, plus external-attenuation-tx and external-attenuation-rx 0..30 dB for patch panel loss, and span-loss-aging-margin-rx 0.00..10.00 dB default 1.0. span-loss-reference selects configured or measured, default measured. Changing span-loss-receive is traffic affecting. Derived read-only values: fiber-length-derived-rx/tx, span-loss-derived-rx/tx, span-loss-alarm-threshold.

The ots-diagnostics name is auto generated by the system on line card provisioning. The format is ots-diagnostics-<chassis>-<slot>-<DWDM Line>, so an RD20TM DWDM line gives show ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line, and a C2ILASGH with two lines gives ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line1 and ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line2. You cannot set the name; only two attributes are settable: nmoper-alarm-reporting (enabled or disabled, default disabled), which when enabled raises the NMOPER alarm on a mismatch between expected-operator and rx-operator, and disabling it clears the alarm immediately and stops the comparison; and expected-operator, up to 32 characters, empty by default. tx-operator is defaulted by the system as <ne-name>-<Dxx>, that is <ne-name>-D00.

ots-r assumes SSMF: required-fiber-type-rx, the required fibre type on the DWDM Line for the Rx fibre, defaults to SSMF, with the same choice list as OTS (AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS, VistaCor). It is only of relevance if control-mode = auto and there is no fiber-connection. The other settable receive-span declarations are fiber-length-rx (unspecified, or decimal64 0..500.0), span-loss-receive (span-loss-info, default 99), external-attenuation-rx, delta-pointloss (not-applicable or -1..3.5 dB, default not-applicable, the fibre contribution to pointloss to be fine tuned in the field), target-power-setting (manual or auto, default auto), plus label, admin-state and alarm-report-control. Read-only: configured-fiber-type-rx, configured-fiber-length-rx, span-loss-at-amplifier, power-actual-rx, connected-reference.

Yes, via the ots-r-auto-otdr entity on ots-r containers, and the default does depend on greenfield. automatic-otdr enables or disables OTDR based automatic fibre check, with default enabled for green field deployments and disabled for in-field SW upgrade. If the Raman card is associated with a base card equipped with integrated OTDR the default is enabled; if the NE has a Raman card not aggregated with the EDFA card the value is disabled. The setting persists over warm and cold restart and over SW upgrade. Disabling during an active test aborts the ongoing OTDR test and releases the amplifier it blocked; disabling with no test running stops further tests until re-enabled. Example: set ots-r-auto-otdr-1-1-dwdm-line automatic-otdr enabled. Progress is in auto-otdr-state (not-applicable, not-available, pass, in-progress, fail, aborted), and loss-calibration-by-otdr is none, rx-only, tx-only or tx-rx, default none.

Use add oxcon-<name> source <value> destination <value> with the two media channel end-points, for example add oxcon-1-80-192262500__1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 source nmc-1-80-192262500 destination nmc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500. Optional on add: label, activation-mode, auto-delete, activation-request-fwd/bwd, direction (two-way or one-way, default two-way), target-output-power-src and target-output-power-dst (decimal64, range -18.00..15.00 dBm, typically 0 dBm by default, -5 dBm for certain Add/Drop cases), and circuit-id. Whether it comes up on its own depends on activation-mode: automatic means the service is activated by the system on creation and deactivated on deletion, and this is the default in the standard L0 mode of operation. In SLTE mode the default is manual and in HSC OLS mode activate-on-create, where you drive activation-request-fwd and activation-request-bwd with activate or deactivate.

The profile-control command applies only to the RD20TM operating in card-mode = slte or slte-backhaul, and runs in Operational Mode only. Syntax: profile-control [type=]<value> [entity=]<value> [direction=]<value> [[profile-data=]<value>]. type is write-attenuation-profile, read-attenuation-profile, create-power-profile, read-power-profile or read-ocm-power; entity is the instance identifier, for example oms-1-8-dwdm-line or nmc-RD20-1-1; direction is tx or rx, and only tx is supported for power-profile. For RD20TM in card-mode = slte the power profile and OCM power are defined at the output of the booster, before the EVOA, not at the DWDM line out port. OMS attenuation data is <StartFreq in MHz>,<SlotWidth in GHz>,<AttnValue...> with values 0 - 25.50 and N = 776 for standardC-band at 6.25 GHz; NMC attenuation allows -10 - 25.50 with N no greater than 32.

Not much. set pump-<name> accepts only three attributes: label (String, length 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance) and alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited, default Allowed). Everything else on the object is show-only: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled or disabled), avail-state (in-service, out-of-service, normal, abnormal, low-power), managed-by (system or user; only user-created facilities can be user deleted) and pump-type. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. To set the power of an individual Raman pump, use the separate pump-power command with target-pump-power.

Use set pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> target-pump-power <value>, where pump-id is the integer number of the pump. target-pump-power is the Raman pump power in dBm and is applicable when the control-mode is manual. Its declared range is -99.00..99.00 dBm, or not-applicable, which is the default; 0 is used for the not-applicable case. If the card is RPBM the target-pump-power must be in the range 12 to 30 dBm. If the value falls outside the operating range of the Raman sled, the alarm PUMP-Fail (STAT FAIL PSTAT) is raised. The allowed ceiling and floor are read back with show pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> max-target-pump-power min-target-pump-power, both decimal64 with 2 fraction digits in range -99.00..99.00 dBm or not-applicable. Also readable: configured-pump-power (derived automatically if control-mode is auto) and actual-pump-power, default -99.

Use show raman-calibration-<name> calibration-state, for example show raman-calibration-1-8. calibration-state displays the state of the automatic Raman gain calibration process: not-available (calibration has not been triggered or no prior calibration has occurred, the default), in-progress (currently running), up-to-date (completed successfully and current), out-dated (stale, due to OTS OLOS, a change in delta pointloss and similar), and fail (ended with a failure). Supporting read-only attributes: last-calibration-timestamp, the time the last automatic Raman gain calibration rpc completed with or without errors, date-and-time or never; additional-info, a string up to 1024 characters giving troubleshooting information when calibration-state is fail or out-dated; intermediate-results; gain-calibration-error, the residual gain error after each iteration in dB; and calibrated-delta-pointloss, the suggested delta-pointloss, -3..3.5 dB.

rsc is the Raman card Pilot Tone facility. The commands set attributes for or show an RSC, in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Configuration is limited: set rsc-<name> accepts label, admin-state (Unlock, Locked, Maintenance, Unknown; default Unlocked) and alarm-report-control (Allowed or Inhibited, default Allowed). What it reports is the pilot tone power in both directions: rsc-power-rx, the received Pilot Tone integrated power, and rsc-power-tx, the transmitted Pilot Tone integrated power. show rsc-<name> also returns supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled or disabled, default enabled), avail-state and managed-by (system or user, default system).

Because of the OMS monitoring-mode. The spectrum facility is only instantiated by the system when the underlying server layer, OMS, has monitoring-mode configured as either non-intrusive or ila-with-equalization; the existence of the managed object depends on that attribute. The object is only of relevance if the DGE2 is intended to be used in the NE. So set the OMS monitoring-mode accordingly and the spectrum object appears. Once present, the only settable attributes are label, admin-state, alarm-report-control and attenuation-setting, a single attenuation value for the entire spectrum in the range 0..30 dB with default 0 dB, editable only if attenuation-control-mode = manual and control-mode = auto-max-pw. The read-only dge-in-use reports true when the corresponding OMS monitoring-mode is ila-with-equalization.

Use the spectrum-control object, which is keyed by name, direction and center-frequency: set spectrum-control-<name>/<direction>/<center-frequency> [attenuation-target <value>] [target-output-power <value>], with add and delete available too. direction is ingress or egress but currently only egress is supported, and egress is the default; center-frequency is the band slice centre frequency in MHz and is managed by the system. attenuation-target is the required attenuation for the spectra, range 0..30 dB, default 0, and is only possible to configure when a Dynamic Gain Equalizer or equivalent is in use (dge-in-use = true). target-output-power is not-specified or in the range -55..55 dBm, default not-specified. Read back with show, which also returns width (0 if no match, or no ILAx card or DGE fibre-connected) and attenuation-actual. Example: set spectrum-control-1-7-dwdm-line2/egress/194943750 attenuation-target 1.

Use the read-only spectrum-monitoring command: show spectrum-monitoring-<name>/<direction>/<center-frequency> [width] [lower-frequency] [upper-frequency] [target-actual-power] [power-actual] [psd-actual]. direction is ingress or egress, default egress, and only egress is currently supported; center-frequency is the band slice centre in MHz, managed by the system. width is the received NMC width in MHz, default 50000. power-actual is the currently received power in dBm, default -99, where -99dBm means the power has not yet been measured by the OCM on the DGE2 card or no power was detected; for egress it is calibrated at the DWDM line port output. psd-actual is the calculated Power Spectral Density in nW/GHz to 2-digit precision, default not-applicable, and does not depend on the spectra width. target-actual-power is the ATPS-calculated target, relevant only when target-power-setting = auto, default -99dBm. Example: show spectrum-monitoring-1-7-dwdm-line2/egress/191968750.

The super-channel object carries a contention-check-status attribute. Values are pending, success, overridden and failk, with default pending. It reports the Contention Check state set via DNA in openwave mode, and it is only applicable if openwave-contention-check is enabled at the super-channel-group level. openwave-contention-check enables the DNA-assisted contention control mechanism in openwave mode; its values are false and true with default false, so contention checking is off unless you turn it on. You can supply contention-check-status on the add: add super-channel-<name> carriers <value> carrier-mode <value> [label] [admin-state] [alarm-report-control] [contention-check-status], and read it back with show super-channel-<name> contention-check-status. The related line-system-mode attribute indicates the L1-to-L0 power control mode on the SCG port and defaults to openwave.

-m is the merge flag. The add command for super-channel-group works in merge mode only: using -m performs a merge, which is a best-effort add. If the target entity does not exist it is created; if it already exists it is updated with any attributes present on the add command, so the command does not fail when the entity is already there. The syntax is: add -m super-channel-group-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <lock|unlock|maintenance>] [auto-in-service-enabled <value>] [valid-signal-time <value>] [alarm-report-control <allowed|inhibited>] [line-system-mode <value>] [openwave-contention-check <value>]. Defaults: admin-state unlock, alarm-report-control allowed, auto-in-service-enabled false, line-system-mode openwave, valid-signal-time 480 minutes (range 1..7200). Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use show supported-carrier-mode-<name>/<carrier-mode> [capacity] [client-mode] [baud-rate] [application] [compatibility-id] [status] [supported-subtypes], available in Operational and Candidate configuration mode. carrier-mode is an acronymized handle indicating the optical carrier line mode 4-tuple, formatted <Capacity><ClientMode>.<Baud Rate><Application ID>, string length 1..15, for example 600E.84P, 100X.73U or 325M.66P. capacity is the net capacity of the optical carrier in gbps. client-mode is the digital client mode mapped into and transported by the carriers within the superchannel, either ethernet or ethernet-otn. baud-rate is the modulated symbol rate and application is the optical transport application ID the mode is optimized for, string 1..15. compatibility-id identifies carrier modes that can be applied simultaneously, status is the state of the carrier mode, and supported-subtypes is string 0..32, maximum 20 elements.

Use show supported-gain-range-<name>/<gain-range-type> [gain-range-min] [gain-range-max], available in Operational and Candidate configuration mode. gain-range-type is the type of gain range and takes low, high or standard. gain-range-min is the minimum settable gain-target for that range type ('standard'/'low'/'high') and gain-range-max is the maximum settable gain-target for that range type; both are of type gain-value with no default, so the actual numeric limits come from the card being queried rather than from a fixed table. The name key is documented as a flag to enable or disable access control with values true/false, default false.

Different power profiles can be supported to reflect different scenarios when using a card.
